analysis_notes.notes: Torah LM2/124 contains zero bechina edges in the dataset (no records with reference=1124 and type='bechina' exist in torahData.js). The source text itself is extremely short — two paragraphs — and contains no bechina language whatsoever (no use of the terms 'בְּחִינַת', 'הוּא בְחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', or equivalent structural-identity language). The entire teaching is a behavioral directive: when a person receives a thought of repentance (הִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה) and yearning for God (הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּת) in some place, he must immediately strengthen that inspiration in that very place — by speaking words of supplication (תְּחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת) or words of yearning aloud or in his heart — and must not wait or move from that place, even if it is not his fixed place for Torah and prayer (מְקוֹם קְבִיעוּת לְתוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה), lest the inspiration cease when he moves. The second paragraph confirms the Rebbe himself was observed following this practice many times. The structure is purely causal (eitza): receiving the inspiration in a place → remaining in that place → strengthening it → preventing its interruption. There are no parallel-nature (bechina) identifications between any of the concepts in this text. Accordingly, no packages can be formed, no gap additions apply, and no new packages are proposed.
